title: Multiple Choice (1 point each)
instructions: Select the best answer for each question.

prompts.question: Which line correctly creates an array that can hold 5 item names when you don't know the names yet?
answers: string[] items = new string[5];
string items = new string[5];
string[5] items = new string[];
string[] items = string[5];

prompts.question: In the line  Item torch = new Item();  what is torch?
answers: An object (an instance of the Item class)
The Item class itself (the blueprint)
A method that belongs to Item
An array of Items
prompts.correct_answer: An object (an instance of the Item class)

prompts.question: Which pair of method headers is NOT a valid overload (the two cannot exist together in the same class)?
answers: void Heal() and void Heal(int amount)
void Heal(int amount) and void Heal(int amount, bool full)
void Heal(int amount) and int Heal(int hp)
void Heal(int amount) and void Heal(string potionName)
prompts.correct_answer: void Heal(int amount) and int Heal(int hp)

prompts.question: Following the method-naming guidance from Writing Good Code, which is the best name for a method that returns whether the Vault door is locked?
answers: IsLocked()
Lock()
vaultCheck2()
DoDoorStuff()

prompts.question: A class makes its health field private but its TakeDamage method public. What is the main reason?
answers: Other scripts can only change health through a safe action (encapsulation)
Private variables run faster than public ones
Private variables cannot be changed at all, even by the class's own methods
So every object of the class shares one health value
prompts.correct_answer: Other scripts can only change health through a safe action (encapsulation)
